rooms.name: Sewer
rooms.major: MUDDLE all characters permanently.

rooms.name: Crossroads
rooms.major: All characters lose a card.
rooms.notes: The single obstacle (green border) is a dark round woven/twig object with small green specks, read as a nest; at card resolution it could also be a stump or crate-like object - check the art. Exit B (red) is beside the left notch of the top bar (0,0), entrance B (green) beside the right notch (7,0).

rooms.name: Passage
rooms.major: All enemies heal 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns.
rooms.notes: No turn matches exactly: the card draws the tile with flat-topped hexes, i.e. the t0 picture turned a further 90 degrees counter-clockwise (the card turned 90 degrees clockwise is t0: web/axe art on 2,0, vines on 4,1-5,1, skull on 5,5, red roots on 0,4-0,5, tile label by 0,6). matchTurns 0 means that; turned the other way it would be t3. Coordinates were read off the turned card and do not depend on this.

rooms.name: Dead-End
rooms.major: All characters suffer 7 damage.
rooms.notes: ORIENTATION: the card draws the tile with FLAT-TOP hexes (columns, not rows), i.e. the t0 picture turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise (270 degrees clockwise, half-way between t4 and t5), so no tN picture matches it. matchTurns 0 is the picture the coordinates were read from after turning the card 90 degrees clockwise (then the rubble near 2,0/2,1, the ice at the lower left and the tile name at the lower left all match t0). Whatever uses matchTurns to orient the room must allow for this. OVERLAYS: 2,2 is a brown cut-wood/rock lump on snow, read as stump (could be a different 1-hex obstacle); 0,3 and 2,3 are clusters of dark grey-green rocks on snow, read as boulder-1 (different art from Trail's red boulder). Entrance A beside the top notch (between 3,0 and 4,0 on t0); exit A beside the right-hand notch at 7,5.

rooms.name: Hallway
rooms.major: All characters consume and spend all items.
rooms.notes: ORIENTATION DOUBT: the card draws G2b turned 270 degrees clockwise (90 counter-clockwise: flat-topped hexes, the long axis vertical, bright end and the G2b mark at the bottom), which is no multiple of 60. It lies exactly between turn 4 (240) and turn 5 (300); matchTurns 4 is a choice, 5 is equally close. Coordinates were read by rotating t0 by 90 degrees counter-clockwise: row 0 is the left column, row 2 the right column, row 1 the middle, x rising from bottom (0) to top (7). Cross-check: the dark wall tab on the card's left side beside 2/5 is t0's top notch at 3,-1. No overlay tiles on the card (the vines are floor art). Entrance A arrow (right side, low) read as cyan 0,3; -1,3 is the next ring hex down.

rooms.name: Road
rooms.minor: Replace 1 normal enemy in the previous room.
rooms.major: Replace 2 normal enemies in the previous room.
rooms.notes: No turn matches exactly: the card draws the tile upright with flat-topped hexes, i.e. the t0 picture turned a further 90 degrees clockwise (the card turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise is t0: tile label by 0,2/-1,3, tab at 3,-1 under exit A, roots by 3,0-4,0 and 5,2-6,2, notch at 6,3 under entrance A). matchTurns 0 means that; turned the other way it would be t3. Coordinates were read off the turned card and do not depend on this. Entrance B (7,1) sits at the short end of the tile next to 7,0/7,2; the t0 picture shows only a slight notch there.

rooms.name: Cabin
rooms.minor: The character who opened the door loses a card.
rooms.major: The character who opened the door loses 2 cards.
rooms.notes: The card draws the tile with flat-topped hexes: it is the t0 picture turned 90 degrees ANTICLOCKWISE (the opposite way to alcove/armory), so no 60-degree turn matches exactly; matchTurns 0 is the picture read from (card turned 90 degrees clockwise matches t0: moss top-right, wooden door at -1,1, dark notches at -1,3 and 5,3, printed tile name bottom-left). Entrance and exit are both lettered A. The two single-hex wooden boxes at 1,2 and 5,2 are read as crate (could be chests); the dark 2-hex piece at 1,3/2,3 is read as table.

rooms.name: Clearing
rooms.major: Characters can no longer consume elements.
rooms.notes: Turn 3 chosen by the weapons art and tile name in the top-right corner of the card. No overlays on the card.

rooms.name: Altar
rooms.minor: Add 3 BLESS cards to the monster attack modifier deck.
rooms.major: Add 7 BLESS cards to the monster attack modifier deck.
rooms.notes: Orientation doubt: the tile art (moss along the top and left, orange glow at the bottom, statue on the right edge low down, notches top/bottom centre) matches t0, but the small printed tile name sits in the card's TOP-RIGHT corner (upside down), where t3 has it; t0 has it bottom-left. Read as t0 on the art; if t3 were right every hex would map (x,y) -> (4-x,6-y) and entrance/exit would swap sides. Overlay names doubtful: the two middle 1-hex obstacles (1,3 and 2,3) are pink stone blocks with a round basin and steps, read as altar; the two at 2,2 and 2,4 are a dark grey square in a gilded wooden frame, read as pillar as the nearest name (could be a pedestal/crate-like piece). All four are separate 1-hex green-bordered tiles.

rooms.name: Armory
rooms.major: All enemies add +1 Attack to all of their attacks.
rooms.notes: The card draws both tiles with flat-topped hexes: each is its t0 picture turned 90 degrees clockwise (no 60-degree turn matches exactly); matchTurns 0 is the picture read from, and both tiles sit at the same turn. On the card a3b and b2b share rows (a3b row 1 = b2b row 1, a3b row 2 = b2b row 2) with a3b (x,y) = b2b (x+4,y). Join: b2b white 3,2 = a3b cyan -1,2; second check: a3b white 0,2 = b2b cyan 4,2, and b2b cyan 3,3 = a3b cyan -1,3. Number 1 sits on the join hex made of the two half-hexes at the notches, cyan on both tiles (b2b 3,1 = a3b -1,1); it is recorded as b2b 3,1 although that is not a white hex of either tile. Three grey-bordered overlay hexes (a 3-hex corridor piece, not listed in overlays because no type fits) cover the join: b2b 3,2 (number 2), b2b 3,1 / a3b -1,1 (number 1) and a3b 0,2 (empty). The two green 2-hex obstacles are weapon racks; shelf is the nearest name. The tiles' small printed names (bottom-left of each when turned) agree with t0. [join set to the seam hex, which the corridor makes a cell]

rooms.name: Encampment
rooms.minor: Upgrade a normal enemy in this room to elite.
rooms.major: Replace an elite enemy in the previous room.
rooms.notes: Turn 0: red floor and bones at the top as in t0. The central 1-hex obstacle (green border) is a ring of sticks/twigs, read as nest; it may be meant as a campfire, which is not in the list. Major text is word for word from the card, though it reads oddly short.

rooms.name: Library
rooms.major: STRENGTHEN all enemies permanently.
rooms.notes: M1a is nearly symmetric under a half turn; turn 0 chosen because the tile mark is at the card's bottom-left as in t0 (turn 3 would mirror every coordinate). The two 1-hex obstacles are dark square blocks read as pillar (stone pillar); could be cabinet/altar. The right bookcase (beside 3) read as 4,3 + 5,4; 5,2 + 4,3 is the alternative one row up.

rooms.name: Den
rooms.minor: All enemies gain "Retaliate 2, Range 3" this round.
rooms.major: All enemies gain "Retaliate 2, Range 3" permanently.
rooms.notes: Turn 3 chosen from the art: blue glow top-left and red stain bottom-left on the card, as in t3. The one obstacle is a small brown coiled/twiggy thing read as a nest; it could be another 1-hex obstacle. Entrance A arrow sits on the left at the row of 9/11, read as cyan 4,3 (5,2 is the next ring hex below-left).

rooms.name: Trail
rooms.minor: All characters spend all spendable items.
rooms.major: All enemies add +1 Move to all of their moves and +1 Range to all of their attacks.

rooms.name: Corridor
rooms.major: STUN all characters.
rooms.notes: The three 1-hex obstacles (green border) are a pinkish stone block with a round basin and a step on one side; read as altar, but could be another 1-hex stone obstacle (e.g. fountain) - check the art. Entrance A at the bottom read by position, same place as Trail's (1,9).

rooms.name: Cave
rooms.minor: The characters who opened the door suffers 6 damage.
rooms.major: The character who opened the door suffers 6 damage and gains STUN.
rooms.notes: Minor text copied word for word including the card's own typo ('characters ... suffers'); it means the one character who opened the door. The three 1-hex obstacles are dark brown rocks on the ice, read as boulder-1 (could be stalagmites). Orientation t0 from the crystals top-left, the sword at the bottom, the right-edge notch at 5,2 and the printed tile name bottom-left.

rooms.name: Tunnel
rooms.major: CURSE all characters three times.
rooms.notes: No turn matches exactly: the card draws the tile with flat-topped hexes, i.e. the t0 picture turned a further 90 degrees clockwise (the card turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise is t0: straight arm with 0,0 under exits A/B, diagonal arm ending in green moss at 7,3-8,4/7,6 under entrance B). matchTurns 0 means that; turned the other way it would be t3. Coordinates were read off the turned card and do not depend on this. Only one entrance (B) and two exits (A, B); the card's corner letter is A/B.

rooms.name: Alcove
rooms.minor: All enemies gain Shield 1 this round.
rooms.major: All enemies gain Shield 1 permanently.
rooms.notes: The card draws the tile with flat-topped hexes: it is the t0 picture turned 90 degrees clockwise, so no 60-degree turn matches it exactly. matchTurns 0 is the picture the coordinates were read from (card turned 90 degrees anticlockwise matches t0 exactly: doors at -1,5 and 7,0, notches at 1,7 and 7,3 all line up). Entrance and exit are both lettered B on the card. Orientation of digits 6 and 9 checked against their positions on the upright card (9 top right, 6 left middle).

rooms.name: Hovel
rooms.major: WOUND all characters permanently.
rooms.notes: C1b on top, B2a below, both at turn 3 (C1b rows 3-4-3-2 from the top with its vines at the top; B2a rows 3-4-3-4 with its mark top-right and its left wall tab at 3,1 beside 5). Join check: c1b 1,0 (6) sits on b2a cyan 1,4 as well as c1b 2,0 (7) on b2a cyan 2,4. 7 and 6 are drawn with grey borders on the card, on the seam between the tiles; I put them on c1b's bottom row (white 2,0 and 1,0), which is also b2a's cyan ring. Exit A arrow (left of 10) read as c1b cyan 3,3; the nearest visible wall notch on that side may be at 4,2 (one row lower).

rooms.name: Burrow
rooms.minor: STUN the character who opened the door.
rooms.major: MUDDLE, POISON and WOUND all characters.
rooms.notes: ORIENTATION: the card draws the two tiles as a vertical strip with FLAT-TOP hexes, i.e. both t0 pictures turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise (270 degrees clockwise), so no tN picture matches; matchTurns 0 is the picture read from after turning the card 90 degrees clockwise (A1a on the left: glowing crack at the top between 1,1 and 2,1, bones and tile name lower left; A2a on the right: skull top-left, tile name lower left). Whatever uses matchTurns must allow for this. The tiles are joined end to end: a2a 0,2 sits right of a1a 4,2 (join); second check: a2a cyan -1,2 = a1a white 4,2, and a2a cyan -1,1 = a1a cyan 4,1. NUMBER 2 sits on the seam hex of the 4-hex rows, made of a1a's 4,1 and a2a's -1,1 - both CYAN, it has no white coordinate on either tile (recorded as a1a 4,1 = a2a -1,1); on the tile pictures that place is drawn as wall. GREY OVERLAY: a 3-hex overlay with a GREY border covers numbers 1, 2 and 3 (a2a 0,2, the seam hex a1a 4,1 / a2a -1,1, and a1a 4,2) - probably a corridor tile laid over the join so the seam hex is open floor; not listed under overlays because grey is not one of the listed types. The obstacle at a2a 2,1 is the same red boulder art as Trail's boulder-1. Entrance B: green arrow at the a1a end of the 4-hex row (a1a -1,1); exit B: red arrow at the a2a end of the 4-hex row (a2a 4,1). [join set to the seam hex, which the corridor makes a cell]
